newsitem.title: USA: Groups sue to block Banc One merger with First USA.
newsitem.headline: Groups sue to block Banc One merger with First USA.

text.p: New York-based group Inner City Press/Community on the Move said Monday it filed a suit seeking to block the $7 billion merger of Banc One Corp and First USA Inc, alleging the Federal Reserve Board's approval of the transaction left its complaints about Banc One's lending practices unresolved.
Inner City Press said it was joined by groups based in Texas and Delaware in the action filed in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit.
On June 13, the groups petitioned for an emergency stay to block the merger, which is scheduled for completion June 30.
Inner City Press said its suit seeks cancellation of the Federal Reserve's May 14 approval of the application of Banc One to acquire First USA.
The motion for a stay asks seeks to block completion of the merger until the petition for review is decided.

Inner City Press said in its filings the Fed erred in approving the merger on condition that Banc One address any weakness in its fair lending polices that may be found in a continuing review. The Fed said it has supervisory authority to address any deficiencies.

In a brief telephone interview, Matthew Lee, executive director of Inner City Press, said a conditional approval was rarely given in bank mergers. He said a problem for the groups is that it is not clear what the condition is.

Inner City Press and other groups had challenged the merger from the start, alleging that there have been unfair lending practices by Banc One and its units Banc One Mortgage Co and Banc One Financial Servcies. The groups alleged Banc One Financial Services targeted minorities for higher-priced credit.
A spokesman for Banc One was not immediately available for comment.
